venue: Delta Center, Salt Lake City, UT, United States

items.fight_news: Natalia Silva and Wang Cong headline UFC 332 for the vacant women's flyweight title, giving the October 3 card a championship centerpiece in Salt Lake City. Silva enters as the No. 1 contender at 20-5-1, while Wang enters as the No. 8 contender at 10-1.

Silva brings one of the division's longest active surges into her first UFC title fight, with speed, movement, and layered kicking at the center of her rise. The broad public read is whether her consistency over three-round fights carries into a five-round championship pace.

Wang's appeal is cleaner than her ranking suggests: she is a sharp striker with finishing power and enough composure to make exchanges feel dangerous immediately. A win would move her from fast-rising challenger to champion in one step.

The main event also starts a new chapter at women's flyweight, because neither fighter is trying to defend an old title reign. This is a fresh belt fight between a long-building contender and a challenger whose striking has made her hard to ignore.

Deiveson Figueiredo vs Payton Talbott is the ranked bantamweight co-main event, with Figueiredo around No. 9 and Talbott around No. 11. Figueiredo enters at 25-7-1 with championship experience from flyweight, while Talbott enters at 11-1 as one of the division's newer ranked threats.

Figueiredo gives the card a proven former champion against a fighter still shaping his top-15 identity. His name value, finishing history, and big-fight experience make this a real step up from ordinary contender sorting.

Talbott is the younger bantamweight with the cleaner recent projection, built around pace, confidence, and offensive comfort. A win over Figueiredo would be his strongest proof that his rise belongs near the division's established names.

King Green vs Esteban Ribovics gives the main card a lightweight veteran-versus-action-fighter slot. Green enters at 36-17-1 with far more UFC experience, while Ribovics enters at 16-3 and has built his reputation on physical exchanges and forward pressure.

Green remains one of the division's most recognizable rhythm fighters, using shoulder rolls, counters, and constant conversation in the pocket. For public users, the question is whether his experience can still slow a younger opponent who wants to make the fight uncomfortable.

Ribovics has the kind of style that can turn a veteran test into a breakout moment. If he beats Green clearly, the win carries more weight than a normal mid-card lightweight result because Green has spent years measuring UFC-level timing.

Khaos Williams vs Roberto Soldic is a welterweight power matchup between fighters with clear finishing reputations. Williams enters at 16-5 and Soldic at 21-4, giving the bout a simple public hook: two dangerous strikers with little room for defensive mistakes.

Williams is familiar as a sudden-damage threat whose fights can change on one clean connection. His UFC run has made him easy to understand for casual users: if opponents give him a pocket exchange, he can end the conversation quickly.

Soldic brings a decorated European profile and a southpaw power game into his UFC debut environment. Beating Williams would immediately tell users that his reputation transfers against a proven Octagon puncher.
Ateba Gautier vs Roman Kopylov rounds out the main card at middleweight. Gautier enters at 11-1 and Kopylov at 15-5, creating a matchup between a rising finisher and a more experienced UFC striker.

Gautier's momentum is built on power and a fast-developing finishing profile, so this is the kind of main-card spot that can accelerate a middleweight name quickly. A convincing win would make him more than an undercard prospect.

Kopylov brings proven striking craft and enough UFC seasoning to ask harder questions than a pure showcase opponent. His public case is that experience, timing, and shot selection can slow Gautier's momentum before the fight turns into a power contest.

Imanol Rodriguez vs Alden Coria opens the prelim run at flyweight, with Rodriguez entering unbeaten at 7-0 and Coria entering at 13-3. The matchup gives the lighter divisions a clean prospect-versus-more-tested-opponent frame.

Rodriguez's undefeated record is the broad hook, but Coria has the deeper professional ledger and more losses to learn from. That makes the fight a useful early-card read on whether Rodriguez's upside is ready for a more experienced pace.

Damian Pinas vs Andrey Pulyaev is a middleweight prelim between fighters with matching physical stakes and different career lines. Pinas enters at 10-1, while Pulyaev enters at 10-5 with more visible adversity on his record.

Pinas carries the cleaner record and the fresher upside, which makes him the easier fighter to project for a fast climb. Pulyaev's value is as the spoiler with enough professional experience to test whether that record has already been stress-tested.

Marcus McGhee vs Benardo Sopaj is a ranked bantamweight prelim, with McGhee holding the No. 15 tag at 11-2 and Sopaj entering at 13-3. It gives the prelims a meaningful 135-pound fight with direct implications for the bottom of the rankings.
McGhee has already shown UFC finishing ability and enough toughness to stay relevant after a setback. Defending a ranking against Sopaj would help keep him attached to the division's next wave.

Sopaj gets a chance to convert a strong record into a ranked result. The public stakes are straightforward: beat McGhee and he likely takes over the kind of ladder position that changes his next booking.

Anthony Wint vs Lucas Armand is a heavyweight prelim between unbeaten fighters, with Wint entering at 8-0 and Armand at 6-0. That kind of record pairing gives the bout instant volatility even before style is considered.

Wint has the slightly deeper pro ledger and is returning quickly to the Octagon, while Armand arrives with a perfect record of his own. The simple public hook is that one undefeated heavyweight record has to absorb its first loss.

Johnny Walker vs Mick Parkin is listed at heavyweight and brings a familiar name into the early prelims. Walker enters at 22-10 with years of high-profile UFC experience, while Parkin enters at 10-1 as the steadier recent profile.

Walker remains a high-variance athlete whose power, length, and unpredictability can make any fight feel unstable. That volatility is the public story against Parkin, who has generally been framed as the more measured heavyweight.

Parkin gets a recognizable opponent at the right moment. A win over Walker would be a bigger name result than his record alone can provide, especially if he handles the early danger without letting the fight become chaotic.

bouts.title: Rafael Dos Anjos vs Alexander Hernandez

items.fight_news: Rafael Dos Anjos vs Alexander Hernandez revisits a lightweight matchup with very different career mileage on each side. Dos Anjos enters at 32-17 as a former champion, while Hernandez enters at 18-9 with the athletic profile of a fighter still dangerous in bursts.

Dos Anjos gives the early prelims a veteran anchor and a familiar all-phase test. Even late in his career, his pressure, clinch craft, and southpaw experience make him a difficult opponent to treat like a simple name fight.

Hernandez has the chance to turn a familiar matchup into a course correction. Beating Dos Anjos would carry more value than a standard prelim win because it would come against a former champion who still asks disciplined questions.

Marvin Vettori vs Ismail Naurdiev adds veteran middleweight depth to the early prelims. Vettori enters at 19-10-1 with years near the top tier of the division, while Naurdiev enters at 25-8 with a broad professional background.

Vettori's public identity is durability, pressure, and stubborn round-winning effort. That makes him a difficult measuring stick for Naurdiev, because opponents usually have to beat him repeatedly across phases rather than win one clean moment.

Naurdiev brings enough experience to make this more than a veteran showcase. His opportunity is to show that his athleticism and striking variety can create separation against a fighter known for dragging opponents into hard minutes.

Court McGee vs Eric Nolan opens the card at welterweight, with McGee entering at 22-14 and Nolan at 8-5. The matchup pairs a long-tenured veteran with a less established opponent trying to use a big platform to reset expectations.
McGee's story is experience and volume over flash. He has seen enough UFC rounds that Nolan will need more than one strong exchange to convince users he can control the full fight.

Nolan has the finishing-leaning profile and the lower-mileage career, which gives him the underdog intrigue. If he can create early damage or force McGee backward, he can make the opener feel very different from a veteran pace fight.
